title: Design a Stack With Increment Operation
description:
Design a bounded stack `CustomStack` that supports incrementing the bottom `k` elements in `O(1)` time.

Implement the `CustomStack` class:
- `CustomStack(int maxSize)` initializes the stack with maximum capacity `maxSize`.
- `void push(int x)` adds `x` to the top of the stack if the stack has not reached `maxSize`; otherwise does nothing.
- `int pop()` pops and returns the top of the stack, or `-1` if the stack is empty.
- `void increment(int k, int val)` increments the bottom `k` elements of the stack by `val`. If there are fewer than `k` elements in the stack, increment all elements currently in the stack.

Every operation (`push`, `pop`, and `increment`) must run in `O(1)` time.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made across push, pop, and increment.
hints: Maintain a parallel lazy-increment array inc[] of the same length as the stack.
For increment(k, val), only add val to inc[min(k, size) - 1]; when popping index i, add inc[i] to the popped value and propagate inc[i] down to inc[i - 1].

examples.explanation: Pushing 1, 2, popping 2, pushing 2, 3, 4 (4 ignored as maxSize=3), incrementing bottom 5 by 100 and bottom 2 by 100 yields [201, 202, 103], popping 103, 202, 201, then -1.
Incrementing an empty stack has no effect and popping returns -1.
With maxSize=1, only the first push succeeds and receives the lazy increment before popping.
